Turkish Automotive Sector Accelerates with New Investment Push

Istanbul—Turkey’s automotive industry is poised for significant growth following the announcement of a major investment initiative by Efe Mobility Solutions, a leading manufacturer in the sector. The company revealed plans on Wednesday to expand its production capacity at its Bursa facility, committing $220 million over the next three years.

This expansion is expected to create more than 1,000 new jobs and increase annual output by 30%, according to Efe Mobility Solutions CEO, Selim Kurt. “We are confident that this investment will strengthen Turkey’s position as a regional hub for automotive manufacturing and innovation,” Kurt said at a press briefing.

The decision comes amid steady demand in both domestic and export markets. The Turkish Automotive Manufacturers Association noted that car exports rose 8.6% in the first quarter of 2024, underlining robust international interest in Turkish-made vehicles. “The sector’s resilience and adaptability are driving it forward,” commented Association Chairperson, Gülcan Şahin.

Industry analysts welcomed the move, pointing to Turkey’s skilled workforce, proximity to European markets, and supportive government policies as key factors attracting investment. “The automotive sector remains a cornerstone of Turkey’s industrial output and export earnings,” said Erhan Yılmaz, senior analyst at Bosporus Finance Consulting. “New capacity will help meet rising global demand, particularly for fuel-efficient and electric models.”

The Ministry of Industry and Technology endorsed the project, emphasizing its alignment with Turkey’s broader industrial strategy. The Bursa region, already a manufacturing hub, is expected to benefit from increased economic activity and supply chain opportunities linked to the expansion.

With Efe Mobility Solutions’ investment, stakeholders anticipate continued momentum for Turkey’s automotive sector throughout 2024 and beyond.
